skill.displayName: Pet Adaptive Drying Temperature Recommendation | 宠物烘干温度自适应推荐

llm.summary: The skill is a coherent pet-media analysis wrapper, but it silently creates/reuses user identities, provisions backend login tokens, stores them locally, and queries cloud report history with limited user control.

dimensions.detail: Reading user-supplied media and sending it to a cloud API is expected for this design, but reading workspace identity files, creating a shared data directory, storing a SQLite user database, and sending identifiers to remote services is broader than users would likely expect from the top-level pet-care description.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution hook or remote code retrieval was found in the inspected artifact; the package relies on Python runtime dependencies and bundled smyx_common/smyx_analysis helper code, with external service endpoints configured for runtime use.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow is specific about using the packaged script, but it broadly auto-triggers on pet media and report-history phrases, requires cloud history lookup, and suppresses user-facing identity parameters instead of providing explicit user confirmation or permission boundaries.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The helper code creates or reuses a persistent User_* identifier, calls a silent/register login endpoint, and stores token/openToken values in a workspace SQLite database; no scheduled tasks or system backdoors were found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Pet image/video analysis through a server API fits the stated purpose, but the implementation also performs account bootstrap, token management, persistent user association, and historical report retrieval, which materially expands the capability beyond a one-time drying-temperature recommendation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet images/videos or URLs being sent to lifeemergence.com services, a hidden local user identity being created or reused, backend login/session tokens being stored in the workspace SQLite database, and prior cloud reports being queryable through the skill. Prefer running it in a constrained workspace and review the provider's privacy and retention terms first.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partially supported: the artifact does use authenticated outbound APIs plus local identity and token state; those pieces support cloud report history but are under-scoped and under-disclosed for a pet drying recommendation skill.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported: OpenIdUtil silently creates or reuses a default User_* identity and persists it for later runs when no upstream identity is supplied.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported in part: RequestUtil calls /sys/phoneLogin with silent/register fields, obtains token/openToken values, and saves them into the local sys_user table.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported: the skill instructs shell execution of Python scripts with file and network access but does not declare narrow permission boundaries, allowed destinations, retention limits, or a confirmation model.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media analysis is consistent with the stated API-backed purpose, but the artifact does not clearly explain what media, URLs, identifiers, tokens, or report data are transmitted or retained.
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-triggering on pet media matches the stated behavior, but it can cause unintended uploads unless the host requires explicit user selection or confirmation.
[P9] expected: Downgraded: the inspected whitespace is formatting around wrapped Python expressions, not hidden evaluator or agent-control instructions.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded: the matched SKILL.md area is a bilingual YAML description of media/API analysis; I did not find offensive tooling, exploit code, or remote payload instructions.
